subtype: Tongue in cheek humour at work [Mismatch]
passage: So Afreen, you asked about the time I joked in my first week. I am Zubin, a QA tester. The team lead said, "The build failed again," and I said, completely flat, "Great, my favourite hobby," with my tongue pressed into my cheek and one eyebrow slightly up. My old team would have laughed. Here, nobody did. One colleague looked worried, like I was really upset. I felt a bit silly, so I smiled and said, "Sorry, joking!" and then everyone relaxed. Now with new people I add a small grin first. Dry humour needs a smile when they do not know you yet. 🙂

qa.q: Why did Zubin add a smile and say "Sorry, joking!"?
qa.a: Zubin saw that the flat remark was taken seriously and a colleague looked worried, so a quick apology showed it was a joke. The blank delivery could have read as sarcasm or real annoyance to people who did not know Zubin.

qa.q: What would you advise Zubin to do with a new team in the future?
qa.a: Zubin could add a small grin to dry remarks until people know the style, as now, and let the humour show more gradually.

qa.q: How did the worried colleague probably see Zubin's remark?
qa.a: They likely took it as real frustration about the failed build, because a tongue-in-cheek look and flat tone can be missed by people who do not know the speaker.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional pairing a tongue-in-cheek face with a dry remark that new colleagues missed until a smile clarified it.

subtype: Tongue in cheek humour at work [Mismatch]
passage: I sat behind Harish in the sprint review when the manager said, "Ojas will present the report, since he loves them." Harish pushed his tongue into his cheek, gave a deadpan look and said, "Best day of his life." I laughed. Ojas laughed too, because they have shared a desk for years. But the new intern, two chairs away, went stiff and looked at her laptop. I could not tell if she thought Harish was being unkind. After the meeting Harish caught her eye and grinned, "That was a joke, by the way, Ojas and I do that." She smiled back, relieved. I am not sure it was needed, but it seemed kind.

qa.q: Who presented the report in the sprint review?
qa.a: Ojas was asked to present the report.

qa.q: How might Harish have felt when he noticed the intern go stiff?
qa.a: Harish was probably a little concerned that his deadpan joke had sounded unkind to someone who did not know him and Ojas, so he grinned and explained afterwards.

qa.q: What could a person do if a dry joke lands badly with someone who does not know them well?
qa.a: They could add a smile or a short word like "joking" and explain, as Harish did, without making a big scene.

qa.q: How might the intern have seen Harish's remark at first?
qa.a: She might have taken it as a real dig at Ojas, since she did not know their history and could not read the tongue-in-cheek face as a joke.

grounding: Observer's account of a young professional's tongue-in-cheek face and dry remark, missed by someone who did not know him until a smile clarified it.
